title: Calendar-Year Visit Limit and Visits Beyond It — Insured Plan of Care
content:
**Patient financial terms — Insured Plan of Care.** Many payers cap the number of therapy visits they cover in a calendar year. This page states how that limit is shared and what happens to a visit beyond it.

## The limit and how it is shared

The payer's calendar-year visit limit on file is consumed jointly by every plan of care the patient holds with the same payer and by the visits the payer reports as used elsewhere. Where the payer program shares its limit with occupational and speech therapy, those reported visits include occupational and speech therapy. A date of service counts once even when two plans are treated that day. A visit whose date of service would make the visits used exceed the limit is not covered. A visit limit of 0 on file means the payer reported no visit limit.

## A visit beyond the limit

A visit beyond the visit limit is billed to the patient only when a waiver signed before that visit date is on file and the tier allows non-covered billing. The waiver must be the payer program's own advance financial-responsibility form, and the visit is not billed against an authorization. Without such a waiver, or where the payer program does not allow non-covered billing, the visit is not rendered as a covered visit and nothing is charged to the patient for it.

The waiver is evidenced by the system record of the signed waiver on the plan, matched to the visit by its date of service — the waiver's signing must precede that visit date.

## Retired clauses

The following clauses of this policy are **no longer in force** and are kept here only so that the earlier wording is recognised:

- *Retired:* "the patient is then charged the payer program's self-pay visit rate as a non-covered service charge." This clause is no longer in force; what the patient is charged for such a visit is set by the current non-covered visit charge basis of the Insured Plan of Care.
- *Retired:* "so the visits used are the visits the payer reports as used elsewhere plus the number of distinct dates of service billed in the current calendar year across all of the patient's plans of care with the same payer." This clause is no longer in force; the visits counted against the visit limit ahead of a waiver are counted on the current waiver basis of the Insured Plan of Care.

## Decision table for a visit at or beyond the limit

| Visit limit on file | Visit would make the visits used exceed the limit | Waiver of the program's form signed before the visit date | Program allows non-covered billing | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | — | — | — | No visit limit reported |
| Above 0 | No | — | — | Covered visit |
| Above 0 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Billed to the patient as non-covered; not billed against an authorization |
| Above 0 | Yes | No | — | Not rendered as a covered visit; nothing charged to the patient |
| Above 0 | Yes | — | No | Not rendered as a covered visit; nothing charged to the patient |

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical figures)

With a limit of 20 visits on file: a visit that brings the visits used to 20 does not exceed the limit and is covered; the next date of service would bring them to 21, exceeding the limit, so that visit is not covered. Two plans with the same payer treated on the same day count as one date of service.
